caption: Six people, one salary, R6 400 groceries. Is that normal or are we eating too much?

slides.title:
How I spend my R29 800
p/m with my in-laws
under our roof
Living in Volksrust
slides.body:
Male, 44
Married, two kids (16 and 11), his wife's parents live with them
Job: Train controller, Transnet
Net salary: R29 800 p/m

slides.title: Rent
slides.includes: 4 bedroom house, so the in-laws have a room
slides.body: We rented the bigger house for them. I would do it again, but I did the sum first.

slides.title: Groceries
slides.includes: Six people, three meals, lunch boxes
slides.body: Six people eat a lot. Pap and meat does not stretch like it used to.

slides.title: Car
slides.includes: Instalment and petrol, Hilux double cab
slides.body: I tell myself I need it for the long shifts. Half the time it sits at home.

slides.title: Family support
slides.includes: My mother's rent and my brother's school fees
slides.body: Black tax is not a line I can skip. It is the one my wife never questions.

slides.title: Braai and drinks
slides.body: I know the number. I still buy the extra ice every week.

slides.title: Everything else
slides.includes: school costs, prepaid electricity, medical aid, funeral policies, stokvel, in-laws' medication, phone
slides.body: Seven line items, R9 330. The electricity is the one that surprised me after my father-in-law moved in with a heater.

slides.title: What's left
slides.body: Out of R29 800. A month with one unexpected bill and I am asking someone for a lift to payday.

slides.title: I stopped guessing
slides.body:
I uploaded three months of statements to Beyond Horizon and it grouped every transaction.

Electricity was higher than I had told anyone.

No bank login needed.
